entries.terms: passed (check) a check has passed when its test came out as its rule requires.

entries.meta: The pinned commit is the full commit hash at which we build, run and quote a system.
entries.name: Pinned commit
entries.terms: pinned commit the pinned commit is the full commit hash at which we build, run and quote a system.

entries.meta: A polynomial commitment is a commitment to a polynomial that the prover opens at any point the verifier picks, with a short proof.
entries.name: Polynomial commitment
entries.terms: polynomial commitment a polynomial commitment is a commitment to a polynomial that the prover opens at any point the verifier picks, with a short proof.

entries.meta: A position is a ranked system's place in its model's table: 1 plus the number of systems placed above it.
entries.name: Position
entries.terms: position a position is a ranked system's place in its model's table: 1 plus the number of systems placed above it.

entries.meta: For the Prompt check, we change one prompt token, and the verifier must refuse the proof (rule).
entries.name: Prompt check
entries.terms: prompt check for the prompt check, we change one prompt token, and the verifier must refuse the proof (rule).

entries.meta: On a system's page, a proof is the file the system sends with each reply for the verifier to check.
entries.name: Proof
entries.terms: proof on a system's page, a proof is the file the system sends with each reply for the verifier to check.

entries.meta: A proof of inference is a set of files that lets a verifier check that a reply is what a committed model produces for a prompt.
entries.name: Proof of inference
entries.terms: proof of inference a proof of inference is a set of files that lets a verifier check that a reply is what a committed model produces for a prompt.

entries.meta: A statement is proved when a sound verifier's acceptance establishes it, under the claim card's stated assumptions.
entries.name: Proved
entries.terms: proved a statement is proved when a sound verifier's acceptance establishes it, under the claim card's stated assumptions.

entries.meta: The prover is the program that makes a proof, and by extension whoever runs it.
entries.name: Prover
entries.terms: prover the prover is the program that makes a proof, and by extension whoever runs it.

entries.meta: A publisher is the organisation that releases a proof system and its documents, or a model and its weights.
entries.name: Publisher
entries.terms: publisher a publisher is the organisation that releases a proof system and its documents, or a model and its weights.

entries.meta: The publisher's words are sentences we copy word for word from the publisher's documents at the pinned commit, each linked to its line.
entries.name: The publisher's words
entries.terms: the publisher's words the publisher's words are sentences we copy word for word from the publisher's documents at the pinned commit, each linked to its line.

entries.meta: Q8_0 is the 8-bit copy and Q4_K_M the 4-bit copy: the original model with its weights rounded to 8 bits, and mostly to 4 bits, by llama.cpp at the level's pinned commit.
entries.name: Q8_0 and Q4_K_M
entries.terms: q8_0 and q4_k_m q8_0 is the 8-bit copy and q4_k_m the 4-bit copy: the original model with its weights rounded to 8 bits, and mostly to 4 bits, by llama.cpp at the level's pinned commit.

entries.meta: Quantization stores a model's numbers in fewer bits, which is cheaper to prove and can change replies.
entries.name: Quantization
entries.terms: quantization quantization stores a model's numbers in fewer bits, which is cheaper to prove and can change replies.

entries.meta: A random oracle is an ideal hash function that gives every new input a fresh, uniformly random output.
entries.name: Random oracle
entries.terms: random oracle a random oracle is an ideal hash function that gives every new input a fresh, uniformly random output.

entries.meta: A system's page prints what a grade comes from at the head of an opened petal's evidence, with "our reading" beside the grade wherever a reading of ours sets it.
entries.name: Read as
entries.terms: read as a system's page prints what a grade comes from at the head of an opened petal's evidence, with "our reading" beside the grade wherever a reading of ours sets it.

entries.meta: Recomputation checks a claimed output by running the computation again and comparing.
entries.name: Recomputation
entries.terms: recomputation recomputation checks a claimed output by running the computation again and comparing.

entries.meta: The relying party is whoever acts on a verifier's verdict, such as a customer, an auditor, a regulator or an inspectorate.
entries.name: Relying party
entries.terms: relying party the relying party is whoever acts on a verifier's verdict, such as a customer, an auditor, a regulator or an inspectorate.

entries.meta: For the Reply check, every proof must cover all of the request's reply tokens, and when we change one of them (the first, the last or one inside), the verifier must refuse the proof (rule).
entries.name: Reply check
entries.terms: reply check for the reply check, every proof must cover all of the request's reply tokens, and when we change one of them (the first, the last or one inside), the verifier must refuse the proof (rule).

entries.meta: A request is one prompt and the reply checked for it.
entries.name: Request
entries.terms: request a request is one prompt and the reply checked for it.

entries.meta: The residual is what a dishonest prover can still do while its proofs are accepted.
entries.name: Residual
entries.terms: residual the residual is what a dishonest prover can still do while its proofs are accepted.

entries.meta: For the Run check, we run the publisher's prover, as published at the pin, for three sessions from a cold start, and every reply must get an accepted proof (rule).
entries.name: Run check
entries.terms: run check for the run check, we run the publisher's prover, as published at the pin, for three sessions from a cold start, and every reply must get an accepted proof (rule).

entries.meta: A guarantee is sampled when it comes from checking a random part of the work, such as some replies.
entries.name: Sampled
entries.terms: sampled a guarantee is sampled when it comes from checking a random part of the work, such as some replies.

entries.meta: A security level measures, in bits, how hard it is to get a false proof accepted.
entries.name: Security level
entries.terms: security level a security level measures, in bits, how hard it is to get a false proof accepted.

entries.meta: The serving baseline is the GPU-seconds per reply that serving the request takes with no proof, on the model publisher's own release.
entries.name: Serving baseline
entries.terms: serving baseline the serving baseline is the gpu-seconds per reply that serving the request takes with no proof, on the model publisher's own release.

entries.meta: A session is one run of a system from a cold start on one slot's prompts.
entries.name: Session
entries.terms: session a session is one run of a system from a cold start on one slot's prompts.

entries.meta: A slot is one of three fixed sets of a model's prompts.
entries.name: Slot
entries.terms: slot a slot is one of three fixed sets of a model's prompts.

entries.meta: SNARK (succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge) and STARK are two names for proof systems.
entries.name: SNARK and STARK
entries.terms: snark and stark snark (succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge) and stark are two names for proof systems.

entries.meta: Soundness is the property that a verifier refuses proofs of false statements, except with a probability the security level bounds.
entries.name: Soundness
entries.terms: soundness soundness is the property that a verifier refuses proofs of false statements, except with a probability the security level bounds.

entries.meta: The soundness error is the probability, as the publisher states it, that a verifier accepts a proof of a false statement, and it is the bound behind soundness.
entries.name: Soundness error
entries.terms: soundness error the soundness error is the probability, as the publisher states it, that a verifier accepts a proof of a false statement, and it is the bound behind soundness.

entries.meta: The statement is the proposition that an accepted proof establishes.
entries.name: Statement
entries.terms: statement the statement is the proposition that an accepted proof establishes.

entries.meta: The steady state is the part of a session after its first group of proofs, when proofs come out at an even pace.
entries.name: Steady state
entries.terms: steady state the steady state is the part of a session after its first group of proofs, when proofs come out at an even pace.

entries.meta: An average is shown above a threshold when our statistical test finds it above at the usual 5% level: p < 0.05 in a paired sign-flip test over the prompts.
entries.name: Shown above
entries.terms: shown above an average is shown above a threshold when our statistical test finds it above at the usual 5% level: p < 0.05 in a paired sign-flip test over the prompts.

entries.meta: Sumcheck is a protocol that convinces a verifier of a polynomial's sum over exponentially many points with one random evaluation.
entries.name: Sumcheck
entries.terms: sumcheck sumcheck is a protocol that convinces a verifier of a polynomial's sum over exponentially many points with one random evaluation.

entries.meta: A theorem is a mathematical result with its proof.
entries.name: Theorem
entries.terms: theorem a theorem is a mathematical result with its proof.

entries.meta: A token is the unit of text a model reads and writes, a word or part of one, stored as an integer.
entries.name: Token
entries.terms: token a token is the unit of text a model reads and writes, a word or part of one, stored as an integer.

entries.meta: Tokens per second is the request's reply tokens over the GPU-seconds one reply took, on one GPU, and the site prints it in tokens/s per GPU with the GPU named.
entries.name: Tokens per second
entries.terms: tokens per second tokens per second is the request's reply tokens over the gpu-seconds one reply took, on one gpu, and the site prints it in tokens/s per gpu with the gpu named.

entries.meta: Trust assumptions is the petal for whether checking a proof relies on anyone's honesty besides the mathematics, such as a setup secret or a hardware maker's key (petal).
entries.name: Trust assumptions
entries.terms: trust assumptions trust assumptions is the petal for whether checking a proof relies on anyone's honesty besides the mathematics, such as a setup secret or a hardware maker's key (petal).

entries.meta: A trusted execution environment (TEE) is a hardware enclave in a processor that isolates code and memory from the machine's owner.
entries.name: Trusted execution environment
entries.terms: trusted execution environment a trusted execution environment (tee) is a hardware enclave in a processor that isolates code and memory from the machine's owner.

entries.meta: A trusted setup is a one-time step that makes public parameters from a secret whose holder could forge proofs, as in KZG commitments.
entries.name: Trusted setup
entries.terms: trusted setup a trusted setup is a one-time step that makes public parameters from a secret whose holder could forge proofs, as in kzg commitments.

entries.meta: Verification is checking a claim against evidence that holds even if the claimant has a reason to cheat.
entries.name: Verification
entries.terms: verification verification is checking a claim against evidence that holds even if the claimant has a reason to cheat.

entries.meta: The verifier is the program that checks a proof against the commitment and the prompt, and accepts or refuses it.
entries.name: Verifier
entries.terms: verifier the verifier is the program that checks a proof against the commitment and the prompt, and accepts or refuses it.

entries.meta: For the Verify without weights check, the verifier must reach every verdict with no copy of the model and no GPU (rule).
entries.name: Verify without weights check
entries.terms: verify without weights check for the verify without weights check, the verifier must reach every verdict with no copy of the model and no gpu (rule).

entries.meta: A model's weights are the learned numbers it is made of, about 8 billion in Llama 3.1 8B.
entries.name: Weights
entries.terms: weights a model's weights are the learned numbers it is made of, about 8 billion in llama 3.1 8b.

entries.meta: A figure of whole sessions counts a session's GPU time from the start of its commit call to its last proof (the commit, generation and proving, but not loading the model before the commit), divided by its replies.
entries.name: Whole session
entries.terms: whole session a figure of whole sessions counts a session's gpu time from the start of its commit call to its last proof (the commit, generation and proving, but not loading the model before the commit), divided by its replies.

entries.meta: The witness is everything the prover uses to build a proof and the verifier does not see.
entries.name: Witness
entries.terms: witness the witness is everything the prover uses to build a proof and the verifier does not see.

entries.meta: Zero knowledge is the property that a proof shows nothing beyond the truth of its statement.
entries.name: Zero knowledge
entries.terms: zero knowledge zero knowledge is the property that a proof shows nothing beyond the truth of its statement.
